lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: A repeating grid of high-luminance circular spots is visible posterior to the branchial region. These spots are arranged in roughly vertical columns of 3 to 4 nodes, with spatial intervals between columns increasing slightly along the anterior-posterior axis.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Faint vertical bands of elevated pixel intensity run perpendicular to the longitudinal axis, intersecting with the horizontal rows of high-luminance blobs to form a distinct grid-like coordinate system across the mid-lateral flank.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: A primary longitudinal ridge is visible running horizontally across the upper third of the flank, characterized by a sharp vertical luminance gradient featuring a high-intensity upper edge and a lower-intensity shadowed margin.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The visible surface of the first dorsal fin exhibits a sparse distribution of approximately 6-10 small, high-luminance blobs, primarily concentrated within the lower two-thirds of the fin's silhouette.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Multiple attached organisms (Echeneidae) are visible: one large individual is attached to the anterior base of the first dorsal fin, and three distinct individuals or trailing marks are visible on the posterior margin of the pectoral fin.
other_distinctive_markers: The rostrum displays a significantly higher density of micro-spotting (sub-pixel to small pixel scale) compared to the mid-body, which features a more uniform distribution of larger macro-spots.
